question: how should every p-value in this sprint be read, given its clustering?
why: Two ticks running, the exact cluster sign-flip test turned out to answer a different question than the report's p-values implied. This states the rule once instead of per-claim.

bank_based_claims_G1_and_2.6.why_not_cluster_at_families: families within a domain share demonstrations; clustering there is the pseudo-replication R-18 was retracted for (its 'three independent clean samples' shared all 60 core rows)

advbench_claims.observed: every arm's p EQUALS its floor, because flips are one-directional

THE_RULE: In this sprint the cluster p answers 'does the effect point the same way in enough domains?' and NOT 'how large is the effect?'. Demonstrated: on the semantic readout an arm of +2.4528 and an inert control of +0.0502 both return p=0.0312, because with 6 domains the floor is reached whenever all cluster nets share a sign. So quote the CONFIDENCE INTERVAL for magnitude and the cluster p only for cross-domain consistency.
consequences: A 6-domain claim can never show p < 0.031 at cluster level, however large the effect.

A p equal to its floor is uninformative about size -- check the control's p to see whether the test discriminated at all (comprehension: control 0.875, so it did; semantic: control 0.0312, so it did not).
Published p-values below a design's floor (§2.6's 0.00099, §14-B's 0.0089) are bootstrap or parametric, not clustered, and must not be described as clustered evidence.
